title: Hermann Graebe's affidavit describes a killing pit at Dubno on 5 October 1942
summary: Graebe's affidavit describes three ditches at Dubno and a reported daily killing of about 1,500 people.
body: Graebe's account, as Fordham prints it, says he was told that some Jews of Dubno had been shot near the building in three huge ditches about 30 metres long and 3 metres deep, and that about 1,500 people were killed daily. The text is one witness's affidavit. It is not a complete ledger of deaths, and a denial was not on this page. The wording on the page includes: "HamburgHaarburg, told me that some Dubno Jews had been shot near the building in three huge ditches about 30 metres long and 3 metres deep. The number of people killed daily was about 1,500. The 5,000 Jews who had lived in Dubno before the Pogrom were all marked for liquidation. Since the executions took place in the presence of my employee, he was". The evidence label is the truth-gate ceiling for this host. The host is not on the gate's primary-text or official list, so the label is weak. The quotation is still the page's wording.
